label: Get node state
description: Read where one node of a run stands: its status, the last answer its wait saw while it waits (an outside job's status, for a progress bar), or its error. Store the run's id with GetRunId when it starts, then read it from any later run. A node inside a loop cannot be read (it fires once per iteration); read the loop instead.

inputs.name: runId
inputs.description: The run to read, by the id GetRunId gave it.

inputs.name: node
inputs.description: The node to read, spelled the way `weft run --from` takes it: `render`, `work.render` inside a group, or `one.render` inside the file the site `one` includes. A loop can be named; a node inside one cannot.

outputs.name: state
outputs.type: { status: String, live?: String, liveTooLarge?: Number, error?: String }
outputs.description: `{ status, live?, liveTooLarge?, error? }`. `status` is one of `pending` (it has not fired in this run yet), `running`, `waiting` (on a signal: an outside job, a person, a timer), `paused` (no wait of its own: its whole run paused while it was inside it, on a bus read or a stream pull, and it carries on when the run does), `completed`, `failed`, `skipped`, or `cancelled` (the run was cancelled before it finished). `live` is there while it waits and its wait has seen an answer: the raw text of the last one (for example the last poll of an outside job's status), for your program to parse. `liveTooLarge` stands in for `live` when that answer was too large for the wait to keep (over 64 KiB): its size in bytes. `error` is the raw error text when it failed.

then.message: GetNodeState '{id}' names {names} in `node`, which has no state a run can tell: no node or loop of this program has that name, it is a group (name a node inside it), or it is a node inside a loop, which fires once per iteration (name the loop instead). Spell a node the way `weft run --from` takes it: `render`, `work.render` inside a group, or `one.render` inside an included file.
